name: Biliary Atresia and Associated Disorders

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in East Asian populations

criteria.description: Persistent conjugated hyperbilirubinemia beyond 2 weeks of age
Evidence of absent or obliterated extrahepatic bile ducts on cholangiography or surgical exploration
Liver biopsy showing bile duct proliferation, portal fibrosis, and bile plugs
Ultrasound showing absent or abnormal gallbladder and triangular cord sign

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent neonatal cholestasis with absent or obliterated extrahepatic bile ducts confirmed by cholangiography or surgery, supported by liver biopsy findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical for timely surgical intervention (Kasai portoenterostomy).

pathognomonic.notes: Cholestatic jaundice persisting beyond 2 weeks of life

searchTerms: acholic stools indicating bile flow problems

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dark urine due to conjugated hyperbilirubinemia

common.notes: Enlarged liver due to cholestasis and fibrosis
Poor weight gain due to malabsorption
Itching due to bile salt accumulation

occasional.symptomName: Coagulopathy due to vitamin K deficiency
occasional.notes: Bleeding tendency from fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption
searchTerms: bleeding problems from vitamin K lack
blood clotting issues due to vitamin deficiency
coagulopathy linked to vitamin K shortage

rare.symptomName: Associated congenital malformations (e.g., polysplenia, situs inversus)
searchTerms: birth defects like multiple spleens or organ reversal
abnormal organ arrangement present at birth

rare.notes: Occasionally present in syndromic biliary atresia

laboratory: Prolonged prothrombin time due to vitamin K deficiency
imaging: Absent or small gallbladder on abdominal ultrasound
Hepatobiliary scintigraphy showing absent bile excretion
genetic: No consistent single gene mutation; some cases associated with genetic syndromes (e.g., POLR3B mutations in syndromic forms)
other: Liver biopsy showing bile duct proliferation, portal fibrosis, and bile plugs
Intraoperative cholangiography confirming absence or obliteration of extrahepatic bile ducts

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of hepatocellular inflammation without bile duct obliteration
Improvement over time without surgical intervention
Characteristic PAS-positive globules on liver biopsy

redFlags: Persistent conjugated hyperbilirubinemia beyond 2 weeks of age
Failure to thrive with progressive hepatomegaly
references: Sokol RJ, Shepherd RW. Biliary atresia: clinical and research challenges for the twenty-first century. Hepatology. 2007.
